title: Lower back
do: Keep moving gently with short walks.
Change position every 30 to 45 minutes.
Strengthen your hips and core slowly over weeks.
dont: Stay in bed for long periods.
Lift heavy loads with a rounded back.
Push through sharp pain.
recover: Walk for 5 to 10 minutes several times a day.
Use warmth if it feels soothing.
Return to normal movement in small steps, adding about 10% a week.
seeDoctor: Numbness or weakness in a leg
Pain after a fall or accident
Loss of bladder or bowel control
Pain that keeps getting worse or wakes you at night

title: Neck and shoulders
do: Keep your screen at eye level.
Take micro-breaks every 30 minutes.
Do chin tucks and shoulder blade squeezes.
dont: Cradle a phone on your shoulder.
Look down at a screen for long periods.
Sleep on a very high pillow.
recover: Alternate short gentle stretches with movement.
Use warmth if it helps.
Check your desk setup (posture screen).
seeDoctor: Numbness or tingling in your arms
Severe headache with neck pain
Pain after an accident

title: Eye strain
do: Follow 20-20-20: every 20 minutes look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Match screen brightness to your room.
Blink often.
dont: Use a bright screen in a dark room.
Rub your eyes hard.
recover: Rest your eyes in palming for a minute.
Use larger text and a little more distance.
seeDoctor: Sudden vision change
Eye pain or redness that persists
Flashes or floaters appearing suddenly

title: Ankle or foot
do: Begin gentle movement early as pain allows.
Add balance work as it settles.
Wear supportive shoes.
dont: Push through sharp pain.
Run or jump on an unstable ankle.
recover: Start with ankle circles, then balance exercises.
Progress to calf raises when there is no sharp pain.
seeDoctor: You cannot put weight on it
Major swelling or bruising
Numbness or the foot looks out of shape

title: Wrists and hands
do: Keep your wrists in a neutral position.
Take micro-breaks and do hand glides.
Use a relaxed grip on your mouse.
dont: Rest your wrists on a hard desk edge while typing.
Type or click for long periods without breaks.
recover: Stretch gently and rest between tasks.
Check keyboard and mouse height.
seeDoctor: Persistent tingling or numbness
Night pain that wakes you
Weakness or dropping things

title: Upper back
do: Open your chest and roll your shoulders every hour.
Support your forearms on the desk or chair armrests.
Breathe deeply into your ribs to ease stiffness.
dont: Slump forward toward the monitor for hours.
Force aggressive twists when your back feels tight.
recover: Do gentle seated cat-cow and shoulder blade squeezes.
Take short walks to let your spine move naturally.
seeDoctor: Pain accompanied by shortness of breath or chest pressure
Numbness or pins and needles around your ribs or arms
Pain following a fall or impact

title: Hips
do: Stand up and walk for a minute every 40 minutes.
Uncross your legs while sitting at your desk.
Do gentle hip flexor stretches and glute squeezes.
dont: Sit in low, soft chairs for long stretches.
Force deep hip stretches that pinch in the front.
recover: Alternate sitting and standing if possible.
Take easy flat walks before adding hills or stairs.
seeDoctor: Sudden inability to bear weight on your leg
Sharp groin pain that catches or locks
Pain after a fall or hip injury

title: Knees
do: Keep your knees gently aligned with your toes when standing up.
Build leg and hip strength with slow, controlled movements.
Extend your legs periodically during long desk sessions.
dont: Tuck your feet tightly under your chair for hours.
Jump or squat deeply into sharp knee discomfort.
recover: Choose flat walking and gentle sit-to-stands to a higher chair.
Increase walking duration gradually by at most 10% a week.
seeDoctor: Your knee locks, catches or gives way
Significant swelling, heat or redness around the joint
Inability to straighten or bend the knee fully

title: Headaches
do: Relax your jaw and drop your shoulders away from your ears.
Drink water regularly and rest your eyes from bright screens.
Take slow belly breaths in a quiet spot.
dont: Squint at small text or glare on your monitor.
Skip breaks when you feel neck tension building.
recover: Dim screen brightness and do palming for 40 seconds.
Try gentle chin tucks and neck releases without forcing.
seeDoctor: A sudden, severe headache unlike any you have had before
Headache with fever, stiff neck, confusion or vision changes
Headache following a head injury

title: High blood pressure
do: Breathe smoothly through every movement without holding your breath.
Choose steady, rhythmic walking and gentle mobility.
Warm up and cool down gradually.
dont: Hold your breath or strain hard during exercises.
Stand up abruptly from folded positions.
recover: Keep daily walks at a comfortable conversational pace.
Sit and rest calmly if you ever feel lightheaded.
seeDoctor: Talk to your doctor before exercise
Chest discomfort, shortness of breath or dizziness
Severe headache or blurred vision

title: Heart condition
do: Follow the pace and activity limits advised by your doctor.
Use the talk test: keep movement easy enough to speak comfortably.
Take longer warm-ups and cool-downs.
dont: Exercise when you feel unwell, dizzy or unusually fatigued.
Push into breathless or high-strain intervals.
recover: Focus on gentle seated resets and easy flat walks.
Stop immediately and rest if you feel any unusual symptoms.
seeDoctor: Talk to your doctor before exercise
Chest pain, pressure, tightness or fluttering
Dizziness, faintness or unusual shortness of breath

title: Pregnancy
do: Move gently with upright posture and steady breathing.
Drink water and keep cool during movement.
Use a chair or wall for balance as your centre of gravity shifts.
dont: Do deep closed twists or hold your breath.
Push to exhaustion or overheat.
recover: Choose short, frequent walks and seated posture resets.
Rest with your feet elevated when your ankles feel tired.
seeDoctor: Talk to your doctor before exercise
Dizziness, headache, chest pain or shortness of breath before exertion
Calf pain, swelling or any unusual pain or bleeding

title: Recent surgery
do: Follow your surgeon or physical therapist's exact movement guidelines.
Start with gentle breathing, eye resets and approved short walks.
Move slowly and stay well within a comfortable range.
dont: Stretch, lift or twist near a healing area without clearance.
Ignore new swelling, warmth or pulling sensations.
recover: Prioritise rest and tiny circulation breaks approved by your care team.
Add gentle mobility only when cleared.
seeDoctor: Talk to your doctor before exercise
Increased redness, warmth, swelling or drainage at the site
Fever or sudden worsening pain
